raw_case_text:
A 55-year-old farmer, male, was admitted to the Intensive Care Unit of the Befelatanana University Hospital in Antananarivo with an altered consciousness. One month prior to his admission, he complained of a moderate and diffuse headache associated with blurred vision. His general condition worsened quickly during the 3 days prior to admission with the onset of fever and confusion. At admission, physical examination revealed a mild fever (38.6 C), but most of the other physiological parameters were within normal limits. Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) was 4/15; the patient presented unresponsive bilateral tight myosis and signs of meningeal irritation, that is, neck rigidity, Kernig, and Brudzinski signs. No focal neurological signs were observed. Chest auscultation revealed crackles of the lower zones on both sides and diffuse rhonchi. A lumbar puncture showed a high opening pressure (35 cm H2O) of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), which was macroscopically limpid. Examination of other systems revealed no apparent abnormalities, and there was no history of long-term medication with corticosteroids, solid organ or stem transplantation, hematologic malignancies, or chronic disease conditions, such as tuberculosis or kidney/hepatic failure.
Initial laboratory investigations of the CSF showed normal white count and glucose and an increased concentration of protein at 288 mg/dL (normal: <40 mg/dL). Blood count showed elevated white cells at 14 x 103/muL (normal: 4.4 to 10.5 x 103/muL) with 91% neutrophils (normal: 42 to 77%) and 7% lymphocytes (normal: 17 to 49%). Other biological parameters were within normal ranges. A rapid HIV serological test (Alere Determine  HIV-1/2, Alere Inc, USA) was negative; RNA HIV-1 viral load (Generic HIV Charge Virale, Biocentric, Bandol, France) was undetectable, and CD4 count (Alere Pima  CD4, Ireland) was 126 cells/mm3. The brain Computerized Tomography scan and chest radiography were normal.
Direct microscopic examination of CSF with India ink showed the presence of a large number of spherical yeasts surrounded by a clear haloed zone consistent with Cryptococcus spp. (Figure 1). A lateral-flow immunochromatographic assay for the rapid and semiquantitative detection of Cryptococcus antigen (CrAg  LFA Immuno-Mycologics, Inc., OK, USA) revealed a low titre (1 : 40) in the CSF and a higher titre (1 : 160) in the serum. Subsequently, the CSF, inoculated onto Sabouraud-chloramphenicol media without cycloheximide, incubated at 30 C, yielded smooth yeast colonies later confirmed as Cryptococcus neoformans var. grubii by matrix-assisted laser desorption ionization time-of-flight (MALDI-ToF) mass spectrometry using Bruker BioTyper instrument. The isolate was correctly identified at the species and varietal level with a log (score) value of spectra of 2.12. The antifungal susceptibility of the isolate was tested retrospectively by using Etest (BioMerieux, La Balme les Grottes, France). The Minimum Inhibitory Concentration (MIC) was determined as the lowest concentration that inhibited 100% and 80% of the fungal growth for amphotericin B and azoles, respectively. The MIC value for amphotericin B was 0.25 mug/mL, for voriconazole 0.38 mug/mL, and for fluconazole 48 mug/mL. The high MIC value of fluconazole was confirmed at 32 mug/mL by the EUCAST reference method (EDef 7.2 Revision). Following antigen detection and direct examination of CSF, the patient was treated immediately with fluconazole (1200 mg/day) via nasogastric tube, but the outcome was fatal after 7 days of treatment with acute respiratory distress and worsening of the neurological status with transition to unresponsive coma.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 55-year-old Malagasy male farmer presented in a coma (GCS 4/15) after a 1-month history of moderate diffuse headache and blurred vision that acutely worsened with fever and confusion over 3 days.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: One month prior to ICU admission in Antananarivo, the patient developed a moderate diffuse headache and blurred vision. Over the 3 days preceding admission, his condition rapidly deteriorated with the onset of fever, confusion, and deep coma.
subjective.past_medical_history: No history of corticosteroid therapy, organ or stem cell transplantation, hematologic malignancy, tuberculosis, or chronic renal/hepatic disease. Farmer by occupation.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for headache, blurred vision, fever, confusion, and coma.

objective.physical_examination: Admission temperature 38.6 C, Glasgow Coma Scale score 4/15, unresponsive bilateral tight miosis, positive meningeal irritation signs (neck rigidity, Kernig's sign, and Brudzinski's sign) without focal motor deficits, and bibasilar lung crackles and diffuse rhonchi on chest auscultation.
objective.routine_investigations: WBC 14 x 10^3/uL (normal: 4.4-10.5 x 10^3/uL) with 91% neutrophils (normal: 42-77%) and 7% lymphocytes (normal: 17-49%). Rapid HIV-1/2 serology was negative and plasma HIV-1 RNA viral load was undetectable; serum cryptococcal antigen lateral flow assay (CrAg LFA) was positive at 1:160; chest radiography was normal.
objective.advanced_workup: CD4+ T-cell count was 126 cells/mm3; brain CT was normal. Lumbar puncture revealed elevated opening pressure of 35 cmH2O, clear CSF with normal WBC count and glucose, elevated protein of 288 mg/dL (normal: <40 mg/dL), abundant encapsulated spherical yeasts on India ink microscopy, positive CSF CrAg LFA (1:40), and Sabouraud culture isolating fluconazole-resistant Cryptococcus neoformans var. grubii (confirmed by MALDI-TOF MS, log score 2.12; MICs: fluconazole 48 ug/mL by Etest and 32 ug/mL by EUCAST, amphotericin B 0.25 ug/mL, voriconazole 0.38 ug/mL).

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis of fatal fluconazole-resistant Cryptococcus neoformans var. grubii meningoencephalitis in an HIV-negative patient with idiopathic CD4+ T-lymphocytopenia (CD4 126 cells/mm3), confirmed by CSF India ink microscopy, CSF CrAg LFA (1:40) and serum CrAg LFA (1:160), Sabouraud culture, MALDI-TOF MS identification, and Etest/EUCAST susceptibility testing (fluconazole MIC 32-48 ug/mL). Treated immediately with high-dose nasogastric fluconazole (1200 mg/day, as amphotericin B/flucytosine were not used/available), but the patient developed acute respiratory distress and unresponsive coma and died on day 7 of therapy.
